title: Total Ankle Replacement
plan_types: All lines of business unless otherwise noted in the Program Exceptions section

criteria.question: Is the planned total ankle replacement system a specific, named FDA-approved device?
Is the patient skeletally mature (closed growth plates / adult)?

criteria.text: ankle pain that limits activities of daily living
criteria.question: Does the chart document ankle pain that limits the patient's activities of daily living?

criteria.text: documented failure of at least 6 consecutive months of conservative treatment (such as physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, splints or orthotic devices)
criteria.question: Has conservative treatment (physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, splints or orthotic devices) been tried for at least 6 consecutive months and failed, with dates?

criteria.text: Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot)
criteria.question: Is there arthritis in the adjacent joints (subtalar or midfoot)?

criteria.text: Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle
criteria.question: Is there severe arthritis of the opposite ankle?
Has the opposite ankle been fused (arthrodesis)?
Does the patient have an inflammatory arthritis such as rheumatoid arthritis?

criteria.text: Extensive avascular necrosis of the talar dome
criteria.question: Is there evidence of extensive avascular necrosis of the talar dome?

criteria.text: Compromised bone stock or soft tissue (including skin and muscle)
criteria.question: Is there evidence of compromised bone stock or compromised soft tissue (skin or muscle) at the ankle?

criteria.text: Severe malalignment (e.g., > 15 degrees) not correctable by surgery
criteria.question: Is there severe malalignment (for example more than 15 degrees) that cannot be corrected by surgery?
Is there evidence of an active infection of the ankle joint?
Is there evidence of peripheral vascular disease?
Is there evidence of Charcot neuroarthropathy (neuropathic osteoarthropathy)?
Has the existing total ankle replacement device failed (e.g., loosening, wear, breakage, dislocation, mechanical complication)?

Reimbursement section: reimbursement for the revision or replacement of a total ankle device is made only if the procedure was initially allowed (a payment condition on the original authorization, not a chart requirement; see guideline notes).

exclusions.text: Total ankle replacement is considered experimental or investigational for all other indications.

notes: Dates: 'Original Effective Date: 02/15/10', 'Reviewed: 03/26/26', 'Revised: 04/15/26'. effective_date follows the example fixture's convention (the Revised date of the current version); reviewed_date is the Reviewed date; the original effective date 02/15/10 is recorded here only.

Lines of business: the header says the guideline applies to all lines of business unless otherwise noted in Program Exceptions. FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines (excluded_plans). Medicare Advantage products: 'No National Coverage Determination (NCD) and/or Local Coverage Determination (LCD) were found at the time of the last guideline reviewed date' - the document does not say MA follows another document, so MA is not listed as excluded; a reviewer should confirm Florida Blue's MA handling.

The position statement is one sentence holding several requirements; it was split into: FDA-approved device, skeletally mature, ankle pain that limits ADL, documented failure of at least 6 consecutive months of conservative treatment, ONE of four conditions, and NO evidence of six contraindications (modelled as not(any(...))).

'using an FDA-approved device' is kept as an answerable criterion: a surgical plan normally names the implant system, and a nurse would ask for the device name if absent. A reviewer could instead mark it answerable: false (FDA status is not a chart fact); the device name is what the chart can show.
'ankle pain that limits activities of daily living' is kept as one criterion (pain is only a requirement insofar as it limits ADL), not split into 'ankle pain' and 'limits ADL'.

'Severe malalignment (e.g., > 15 degrees) not correctable by surgery': the threshold > 15 degrees is given as an example (e.g.) of severe, so it is recorded as the threshold but is illustrative; malalignment that is correctable by surgery is not a contraindication even if > 15 degrees.

The NOTE 'Optimal candidates for total ankle replacement are considered to be older (age older than 50), thin, low-demand individuals with minimal deformity and no functional barriers to participation in a rehabilitation program' is deliberately left out of the tree: it describes optimal candidates and is not a requirement (no age, BMI or demand threshold is imposed).

Revision/replacement pathway: 'all medical necessity criteria outlined above (excluding 6 consecutive months of conservative treatment)' is read as every primary criterion except the 6-month conservative treatment trial, including skeletal maturity, ankle pain limiting ADL, ONE of the four conditions and NO evidence of the six contraindications. A reviewer could argue the 'ONE of the following conditions' list was written for primary arthritis indications and sits oddly with a failed implant, but the document says 'all' and lists only one exclusion.

'Revision or replacement of the implant, using an FDA-approved device' reuses the fda_approved_device criterion; the same words 'using an FDA-approved device' appear in both the primary and the revision sentences.

REIMBURSEMENT INFORMATION: 'Reimbursement for the revision or replacement of a total ankle device is made only if the procedure was initially allowed.' Deliberately left out of the tree: it is a payment condition about the payer's own prior authorization history, outside the Position Statement, and not something a chart documents. A reviewer could instead add it to the revision pathway as an answerable: false criterion.

The LOINC documentation table and the sentence 'The following information may be required documentation to support medical necessity: Physician history and physical, attending physician treatment plan, progress notes, and treatment notes including documentation of symptoms, failure of at least 6 consecutive months of conservative treatment, and radiology reports (if applicable)' describe what records to submit (observations six months or fewer before the date of service), not additional criteria; left out.

ICD-10 codes are listed as 'Diagnosis Codes That Support Medical Necessity'; they are recorded in scope.icd10 as printed and are not a criterion. The T84.0x8 ranges (prosthesis complications) correspond to the revision pathway and the M-codes to the primary pathway, but the document does not assign codes to pathways.

Both CPT codes are tagged covered: 27702 (primary TAR) is governed by the primary pathway and 27703 (revision) by the revision pathway. The investigational statement 'for all other indications' does not make either code non-covered; it is recorded as an exclusion with no codes.
The six 'NO evidence of' items are contraindications inside the medical necessity statement, so they live in the tree as not(any(...)) and are not repeated in exclusions.
The step therapy protocol exemption paragraph (Florida law 627.42393) is an administrative right to request an exemption, not a criterion; left out.
DESCRIPTION, DEFINITIONS (arthrodesis, Charcot neuroarthropathy), RELATED GUIDELINES, REFERENCES and update history hold no requirements.
